question_text: A 0.4-m (15.7-in.) rod of a metal elongates 0.48 mm ( 0.019 in.) on heating from $20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\left(68^{\circ} \mathrm{F}\right.$ to $212^{\circ} \mathrm{F}$ ). Determine the value of the linear coefficient of thermal expansion for this material.The unit of the answer is C^-1.
response:
The linear coefficient of thermal expansion is defined by:

$$\Delta L = \alpha L_0 \Delta T$$

Solving for $\alpha$:

$$\alpha = \frac{\Delta L}{L_0 \Delta T} = \frac{0.48\times10^{-3}\ \text{m}}{(0.4\ \text{m})(100-20)\ ^\circ\text{C}} = \frac{0.48\times10^{-3}}{32} = 1.5\times10^{-5}\ ^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$$

$$\boxed{1.5\times10^{-5}}$$
